root_cause: _hex_nexorade_core's face_ring(a,b,c) returned the MAX axial ring (0=centre) of a triangular face's 3 vertices, clamped to [0,rings], and group_ring_cap defaulted to rings+1 (one section-group family per ring INCLUDING a ring-0 'centre' family). But a triangular face can never have all 3 vertices at axial ring 0 -- there is exactly one node at ring 0 (the hex-grid's centre point), and 3 distinct nodes are needed to form a face -- so face_ring() could structurally never return 0 for any real face, for ANY (rings, edge) combination. Ring-family 0 (group indices 0,1,2 of every hex_nexorade/rf_dome model) was therefore always-empty by construction, not a parameter-specific accident: verified analytically (face_ring range check) and numerically (face_ring distribution for rings=1..6, minimum observed ring is always 1) below. For CS3's hex_nexorade(3, 2.2, 0.25): n_groups was reported as (rings+1)*3=12, but only ring families 1,2,3 (9 groups) ever carry a beam element; groups 0,1,2 (ring family 0) are permanently empty, inflating CS3's F1 sizing QUBO by 3 groups x 8 CHS sections = 24 phantom (structurally inert) qubits, from a true 9*8=72 to a reported 12*8=96.
fix: code/reciprocal_geom_v2.py _hex_nexorade_core: face_ring(a,b,c) now returns (min(int(r), rings) - 1), shifting the family index to a contiguous 0-based range [0, rings-1] with no unreachable leading family; group_ring_cap now defaults to `rings` (was `rings+1`) when max_group_rings is None. n_groups = group_ring_cap*3 is unchanged as a formula -- it now correctly evaluates to the TRUE active group count. Geometry (node coordinates, element i/j connectivity, support_idx, load_idx) is bit-for-bit UNCHANGED by this fix -- verified by rebuilding hex_nexorade(3,2.2,0.25) under the pre-fix and post-fix face_ring() definitions side by side: identical node list, identical element list (comparing every element's i/j/kind/member_id, ignoring only the group label), identical support_idx and load_idx. Every beam element's group label is uniformly shifted by exactly -3 (i.e. -1 per ring family x 3 groups/ring), a pure relabeling consistent with removing exactly the one always-empty leading ring family. lam_per_ring (used only by the deprecated/superseded rf_dome and rf_dome_complex, not by any current headline generator) is unaffected in practice: its docstring length convention is updated from `rings+1` to `rings`, but since the previous index 0 was already dead code (face_ring never returned 0), no caller passing a list of length rings+1 or rings can go out of bounds either way -- purely a documentation/consistency correction.

hex_nexorade(3,2.2,0.25)_CS3_AFTER_FIX.note: n_groups now 9 (was 12); all 9 groups active/non-empty; 240 beam elements total, unchanged from before the fix; sizing QUBO is now 9*8=72 bits (was 96) -- 24 phantom bits removed.

face_ring_defect_sweep_rings_1_to_6.description: Raw (pre-fix) face_ring() distribution vs `rings`, for hex_nexorade's own edge=2.2. Ring value 0 NEVER occurs at any rings -- proof the empty-ring-0-family defect is structural, present for every valid (rings, edge).

rf_dome_old_superseded_note: rf_dome (old, non-'2' generator, shares _hex_nexorade_core with hex_nexorade) inherits the identical fix by construction (same shared function) but is NOT part of any currently-headline case study: CS4's geometry search (cs4_dome2.py) and dome-fixed sizing (dome2_sizing.py) were already migrated to rf_dome2 (a different, annulus-indexed ring family that starts at a real ring-0 by construction -- see below, confirmed clean) well before this audit. rf_dome/rf_dome_complex remain importable only for deprecated/superseded historical scripts (cs4_v2.py, r6_uls_v2.py's old recover_cs4, review_rd/re/rh, cs4_complex.py/dome_sizing.py's rf_dome_complex path) whose output files are not cited in results_v2/complex_summary.md or the current manuscript headline numbers; not re-run as part of this fix.

rf_dome2(n_sect=7,n_ring=4,max_group_rin.verdict: CLEAN -- no empty groups. rf_dome2 keys ring family by the ANNULUS index between successive rings (0=innermost annulus, touching the apex node), which is a real, populated face family from i=0 by construction (unlike hex_nexorade's per-VERTEX ring, whose ring-0 is a single unreachable apex point) -- structurally immune to this defect.
